core_obligations: Construct inner edges near nontrivial p-th rotations, and cross edges by a prescribed complex phase sector with narrow imaginary-part strips removed.
Show any large inner set contains p nearby rotated points, transfer them to distinct partition representatives, and simultaneously exclude (p+1)-cliques and bound inner degree.
Control degree for every vertex via measure of phase sectors and angular perturbation when a continuum point is replaced by a cell representative.

Exclude a (p+ell+1)-clique: a majority of rotation classes has zero in its planar convex hull, producing a small convex combination; a far rotation pair on the other side then gives incompatible upper and lower imaginary-part estimates.

Obtain a far-rotation pair and carry out the convex-hull imaginary-part contradiction.

difficulty_reason: The counted result is the full construction, not a local triangle-inequality lemma. It must make four competing global properties hold at once: asymptotically prescribed rational cross density, vanishing inner density, sublinear p-independence, and a sharp forbidden mixed clique. The new mechanism is the coupling of root-of-unity near-rotations to a complex phase window; the final mixed-clique obstruction combines planar convexity with a signed imaginary-part estimate. Standard concentration bounds alone provide none of this construction. H3 is a provisional initial assessment requiring two independent substantive reviews of this same complete unit.

compared.difference: The old primary is a weighted-graph upper-bound subproblem. The proposed counted unit is the full complex-sphere lower-bound construction with prescribed rational cross density.
